title: Const-generic wire format is well-designed
description:
The use of const generics `<M, N, T, TILE>` for SCHC parameters (wire.rs, all fragmentation modules) is genuinely well done:

```rust
pub struct Fragment<'a, const M: u8, const N: u8, const T: u8> { ... }
pub struct Ack<const M: u8, const N: u8, const T: u8> { ... }
pub struct AckOnErrorSender<'a, const M: u8, const N: u8, const T: u8, const TILE: usize> { ... }
```

Benefits:
1. Compile-time validation of parameter combinations
2. Constants like `FCN_MAX`, `WINDOW_SIZE` are computed at compile time
3. The compiler can optimize away bounds checks when TILE is known
4. No runtime storage of parameters
5. Type aliases (`lorawan::Fragment`, `lorawan::Sender`) provide ergonomic presets

This is worth defending if someone suggests "simplifying" to runtime parameters - the const-generic approach is the right choice for a protocol library targeting embedded.
